verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ aññataro bhikkhu kosalesu viharati aññatarasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe.
verses.english: At one time one of the mendicants was staying in the land of the Kosalans in a certain forest grove.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena so bhikkhu yaṁ sudaṁ pubbe ativelaṁ sajjhāyabahulo viharati so aparena samayena appossukko tuṇhībhūto saṅkasāyati.
verses.english: Now at that time that mendicant had previously been spending too much time rehearsing. But some time later they adhered to passivity and silence.

verses.pali: Atha kho yā tasmiṁ vanasaṇḍe adhivatthā devatā tassa bhikkhuno dhammaṁ asuṇantī yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṁ bhikkhuṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
verses.english: Not hearing the teaching, the deity haunting that forest approached that mendicant, and addressed them in verse:
“Mendicant, why don’t you recite <j>passages of the teaching,
Hearing the teaching, one garners confidence;
and in this very life, one garners praise.”
“I used to be zealous for <j>passages of the teaching,

verses.pali: Yaṁ kiñci diṭṭhaṁva sutaṁ mutaṁ vā;
verses.english: whatever was seen, heard, and thought,
this, good people say, <j>is the laying down by complete understanding.”
